claims: above324_refined/ holds sixteen exact rational certificates nNNNN.cert, at 632, 637, 655, 684, 685, 744, 750, 756, 805, 814, 918, 921, 924, 935, 970 and 989, in the format of the above324/ folder: two comment lines, the second 'public competition packing, re-optimized', then 'n S' with S an exact decimal fraction, then n rows 'x y t'. #942 and above324_refined/README.md print each side rounded up at 10 places: 632 25.6456954277, 637 25.7447388658, 655 25.9996711101, 684 26.6456964776, 685 26.6870020013, 744 27.7601633593, 750 27.8595204745, 756 27.9245802503, 805 28.8450303356, 814 28.9549571055, 918 30.7867372035, 921 30.8271449853, 924 30.8553857463, 935 30.9800571865, 970 31.6389903231, 989 31.8889473785, each below the best value the author could find in this repository at commit f54ad104 and below the best public packing of the Kaggle competition 'Squares in Squares' the author could find, whose values the issue prints beside them.

The issue says all 1000 packings of the source file were tested for a remaining descent direction with a linear program on the contact constraints, that sixteen still had one, that following the descent to convergence gave these values with the arrangements of the squares unchanged, and that each certificate carries a margin of about 5e-9 above the numerical optimum.

verify_cert.py, byte-identical to above324/verify_cert.py, checks containment and a separating-axis test in fractions.Fraction; the issue says a second script with separate code checked the same packings in the same arithmetic, that the checkers share one author, the separating-axis test and Fraction, and that the certificates were not replayed with this repository's checkers. The descent test, local optimization, rational certificates and checks were produced with Claude (Anthropic) under Joost de Winter's direction, the issue says. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
